title: Doublet events: global versus within-page shuffle controls
reader_title: Do patterns in the repeated pairs survive shuffling?
reader_intro: A doublet is an identical neighboring rune pair. Its repeated symbol forms one entry in an 86-rune list. This check asks whether reported patterns still stand out when shuffles preserve each page’s own entries and can also choose their best-looking pattern.

reader_test.input: The fixed list of 86 repeated-pair symbols from LP2-00–55, in page order, and three previously reported alphabet-distance measurements.
reader_test.action: Shuffle the entire list 20,000 times, then shuffle only within each page 20,000 times. Compare entries one to three list positions apart; let each shuffle choose its strongest alphabet-distance group too.
reader_test.check: Compare the reported patterns with both sets of shuffles, before and after allowing that choice. These controls keep observed symbol counts; they do not simulate a cipher or cover every pattern previously searched.

question: Do the reported doublet-event distances survive controls that preserve the page-specific event inventory and account for selecting an attractive bin?
summary: The lag-one distance sum is rare under a global event shuffle but ordinary when each page keeps its event symbols. The selected lag-three +4 bin is rare narrowly; choosing the strongest bin across lags gives a much weaker comparison.

scope.representation: One zero-based GP index per overlapping within-page doublet, headings included; remove non-runes and concatenate events in page order.
scope.procedure: Compare three source-specified statistics on the 86-event sequence with 20,000 seeded global shuffles and 20,000 within-page shuffles; also score the largest directed bin and largest three circular bins across lags 1–3.
scope.parameters: Seed 33012026; 20,000 draws per control; one-sided greater-or-equal tails; lags 1–3; 29 directed and 15 circular bins; page event multisets held fixed in the conditioned control.
scope.exclusions: Original unpublished event list and code, other transcriptions, unseen page subsets, all unreported model searches, cipher inference and confirmatory significance claims.

finding: For the observed lag-one sum 734, 31/20,000 global shuffles and 3,910/20,000 within-page shuffles meet or exceed it. The observed +4 count 10 has 13 and 23 narrow exceedances, but allowing selection of any directed bin at lags 1–3 gives 1,123 and 3,510 exceedances.
limitations: The reported statistics and bins were selected after looking at data. These two randomizations are conditional reference models, not models of every plausible encryption process; source p-values cannot be exactly recovered without its inputs and implementation.
next_steps: Obtain the source event list and permutation implementation to locate counting differences; require any proposed +4 mechanism to predict a held-out page or a different untouched statistic.
